thm-ip-truncated-estimator-exact-risk.full_current_section:
Assume Countable Choice and let $\epsilon\ge0$. In the Gaussian sequence inverse model with positive singular numbers $(s_j)_{j\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$, let $Q\ge0$ and let $(a_j)_{j\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$ be positive and nondecreasing. For each $\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)$, define the squared sequence risk of the cutoff estimator at $D\in\mathbb N_0$ by
$$R_\theta(D):=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\|\widehat\theta_D(Z)-\theta\|_{\ell^2}^2\right].$$
Then its exact worst-case squared sequence risk is
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)}R_\theta(D)=\frac{Q^2}{a_{D+1}^2}+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2},$$
where the sum is $0$ for $D=0$. The supremum is attained by the one-coordinate truth $\theta^\star=(Q/a_{D+1})e_{D+1}$, with $\theta^\star=0$ when $Q=0$.

def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model.full_current_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear operator of infinite rank, viewed as an inverse model with exact datum $Kx$. Here compact means that the image of every bounded subset has compact closure. Write $N(K)=\{x\in X:Kx=0\}$ and $H_0=\overline{\operatorname{ran}K}$. Fix a positive singular system $(s_j,v_j,u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$ for $K$, where $\mathbb N_{>0}=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, $s_1\ge s_2\ge\cdots>0$, $s_j\to0$, $Kv_j=s_ju_j$, $(v_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $N(K)^\perp$, and $(u_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $H_0$. A complete orthonormal basis is an orthonormal family whose closed linear span is the whole indicated subspace. These are the compact SVD conventions; in particular, this model concerns minimum-norm representatives in $N(K)^\perp$ and does not estimate a kernel component.

For a truth $x\in N(K)^\perp$, let $\theta_j=\langle x,v_j\rangle_X$. The complete-basis coefficient map identifies $N(K)^\perp$ bijectively and isometrically with $\ell^2(\mathbb N_{>0},\mathbb R)$, so every $\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N_{>0},\mathbb R)$ is a model parameter. For $\epsilon>0$, take the functional white-noise experiment on the separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with observations $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_Y+\epsilon W(g)$, where $W$ is centered, has covariance $\mathbb E[W(g)W(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_Y$, and has independent standard-normal values on every finite orthonormal tuple. The countable complete basis makes $H_0$ separable. Define $\xi_j=W(u_j)$ and $Z_j=Y_x(u_j)/s_j$. The sequence sample space is $\mathbb R^{\mathbb N_{>0}}$ with the product Borel sigma-algebra, meaning the sigma-algebra generated by its coordinate projections. The coordinate law is the pushforward of the functional experiment under $y\mapsto(y(u_j)/s_j)_{j\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$; this map is measurable because each coordinate is a cylinder evaluation followed by scalar multiplication. The compact SVD expansion gives $\langle Kx,u_j\rangle_Y=s_j\theta_j$, and the positive-noise white-noise coordinate theorem gives the independent standard-normal coordinates $\xi_j$. Hence the normalized coordinates satisfy $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j,\qquad j\in\mathbb N_{>0}.$

For the zero-noise boundary $\epsilon=0$, define the sequence experiment separately by the point mass at $\theta$, so $Z_j=\theta_j$. This boundary is not an instance of the positive-noise functional experiment.
def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model.finding: Positive-index notation is made explicit throughout; the normalized coordinate law, variance and separately defined zero-noise boundary support each current Fact unchanged.

def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class.full_current_section:
Let $Q\in[0,\infty)$ and let $a=(a_j)_{j\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$ be a nondecreasing sequence of positive real numbers, so $0<a_1\le a_2\le\cdots$. The statistical ellipsoid of radius $Q$ and weights $a$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse model is
$$\Theta_a(Q)=\left\{\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N_{>0},\mathbb R):\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\right\}.$$
No assumption that $a_j\to\infty$ is included. In particular, this definition does not assert that the ellipsoid is compact in $\ell^2$.
def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class.finding: Positive-index notation changes only; the current Facts use the same positive nondecreasing weights and weighted square-sum class.

def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budge.full_current_section:
Fix a measurable space $(E,\mathcal E)$ and a bounded measurable functional
$f:E\to\mathbb R$, with $\|f\|_\infty:=\sup_{x\in E}|f(x)|<\infty$. All
target laws below are probability measures on this same space. If a model or
discretization originally uses another state space, specify its measurable
embedding into $E$ and compare its pushforward law; no identification of
different state spaces is implicit. A **posterior law** here is the probability
law for the unknown at the specified computation stage, conditional on the same
fixed observed data. For a probability law $\mu$, write
$\mu(f):=\int_E f\,d\mu$.

Name the successive posterior laws as follows: $\mu_\star$ is the intended
target; $\mu_{\rm model}$ is the posterior under the selected statistical or
physical model; $\mu_{\rm solver}$ is the posterior after replacing the exact
forward or PDE solution by the declared numerical solver output; and
$\mu_{\rm disc}$ is the posterior after the declared finite-dimensional
discretization. These labels refer to the exact adjacent laws recorded for the
computation, even when two stages happen to agree.

Let $K$ be the implemented probability kernel on $(E,\mathcal E)$. An
**invariant law** $\pi_K$ for $K$ is a probability measure satisfying
$$\int_E K(x,A)\,\pi_K(dx)=\pi_K(A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal E).$$
Choose and report which invariant law is used if $K$ has more than one. If no
invariant law has been established, the invariant-kernel and burn-in terms
below are unavailable; they are not set to zero. Let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a
time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $K$ relative to its
natural filtration, with initial probability law $\lambda$. For burn-in length
$b\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and retained sample size $N\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, set
$$\bar f_{b,N}:=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N f(X_{b+j}),$$
and let $\mathbb E_\lambda$ denote expectation under this initial law and the
chain's transition randomness.

When all stages are present, define the component errors
$$\begin{aligned}\delta_{\rm model}&:=|\mu_\star(f)-\mu_{\rm model}(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm solver}&:=|\mu_{\rm model}(f)-\mu_{\rm solver}(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm disc}&:=|\mu_{\rm solver}(f)-\mu_{\rm disc}(f)|,\\ \delta_K&:=|\mu_{\rm disc}(f)-\pi_K(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm burn}&:=|\pi_K(f)-\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N}|,\\ \delta_{\rm MC}&:=|\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N}-\bar f_{b,N}|.\end{aligned}$$
The last component is random and the earlier components are fixed for the
declared data and computation. The **posterior computation error budget** is
$$\mathcal B_f:=\delta_{\rm model}+\delta_{\rm solver}+\delta_{\rm disc}+\delta_K+\delta_{\rm burn}+\delta_{\rm MC}.$$
If a computation stops before one of these stages, report the shorter reference
chain and its component terms. The term $\delta_K$ measures the invariant-law
discrepancy induced by the implemented transition rule; it is not a one-step
distance between kernels. A one-step kernel error cannot replace it without a
separate perturbation theorem with its own hypotheses.

The successive scalar references are arranged as this directed error chain;
each arrow is labelled by the absolute difference of its endpoints.

```tikzcd
\mu_\star(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm model}"] &
\mu_{\rm model}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm solver}"] &
\mu_{\rm solver}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm disc}"] &
\mu_{\rm disc}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_K"] &
\pi_K(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm burn}"] &
\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N} \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm MC}"] &
\bar f_{b,N}
```

The budget is a bookkeeping bound only when its components are supplied with
estimators or verified bounds; an unavailable component is reported as
unquantified rather than silently set to zero. In particular, invariance alone
does not provide a burn-in estimate, a mixing rate, or a Monte Carlo error
estimate.

def-ip-anisotropic-conductivity-dirichle.full_current_section:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary. Write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Define the boundary trace-data space $\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ with quotient norm. If $\Omega\ne\varnothing$, its boundary is nonempty, and the trace-quotient lemma identifies this quotient with the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data convention of the scalar conductivity map. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then $H^1(\Omega)=H_0^1(\Omega)=\{0\}$ and the fixed-atlas empty-boundary convention $H^{1/2}(\varnothing)=\{0\}$ gives the identification directly. Let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite, so some $0<c\le C<\infty$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le \xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in\overline\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal B_\Omega$, a weak solution with boundary datum $f$ is a class $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and

$$\int_\Omega \gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

The weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map is the bilinear-form candidate $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega\to\mathbb R$ given, whenever the weak solution exists, by

$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle:=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx,$$

where $V_h\in H^1(\Omega)$ is any representative of $h$. The local anisotropic conductivity well-posedness lemma proves existence and uniqueness for every boundary class, independence of the representative $V_h$, and boundedness on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$; it therefore makes this candidate a bounded bilinear map. The map is the boundary energy form for the equation $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u)=0$. Under the trace-quotient isomorphism and the local boundedness result, this form gives the usual weak map into the dual $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ with the scalar convention.
def-ip-anisotropic-conductivity-dirichle.finding: Empty-domain trace convention is explicit; the consumer uses the nonempty unit ball with n>=3 and full AC (hence CC). Its energy-form Fact is unchanged.

def-ip-pde-solver-admissibility-contract.full_current_section:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ of $\Omega$, and unisolvent reference finite elements assembled on that mesh. Thus the mesh is a finite face-to-face cover by nondegenerate affine simplices with disjoint interiors, and each local finite-element degree-of-freedom map is bijective on its finite-dimensional shape-function space. Fix coefficient spaces $\Theta_h=\mathbb R^m$, $V_h=\mathbb R^n$, and $Y_h=\mathbb R^s$ with their standard Euclidean inner products, where $m,n,s\ge1$. Let $Q_h\subseteq\Theta_h$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $O_h\subseteq\Theta_h$ be open with $Q_h\subseteq O_h$.

A **finite-element PDE model** in this contract consists of a continuously differentiable residual map $R_h:O_h\times V_h\to V_h$ and a continuously differentiable observation map $G_h:O_h\times V_h\to Y_h$. It must supply a continuously differentiable state branch $S_h:O_h\to V_h$ satisfying $R_h(q,S_h(q))=0$ for every $q\in O_h$. For every $q\in Q_h$, this branch must be the specified unique admissible state and the matrix $D_uR_h(q,S_h(q))$ must be invertible. The discrete forward map is $F_h(q):=G_h(q,S_h(q))$. The unisolvent finite-element degrees of freedom identify $V_h$ with its coefficient space; all matrix transposes below are in the fixed Euclidean coefficient inner products.

For data $y^\delta\in Y_h$, reference parameter $q_0\in\Theta_h$, and $\alpha>0$, the discrete nonlinear Tikhonov objective is
$$
\Phi_h(q):=\frac12\|F_h(q)-y^\delta\|_{Y_h}^2+\frac\alpha2\|q-q_0\|_{\Theta_h}^2\qquad(q\in Q_h).
$$
Define the finite-dimensional objective before eliminating the state by
$$
J_h(q,u):=\frac12\|G_h(q,u)-y^\delta\|_{Y_h}^2+\frac\alpha2\|q-q_0\|_{\Theta_h}^2.
$$
The symbols $\nabla_uJ_h$ and $\nabla_qJ_h$ denote the Euclidean gradient vectors representing the two partial derivative functionals. At an admissible $q$, the **exact discrete adjoint** $p_h(q)\in V_h$ is the unique solution of
$$
\bigl(D_uR_h(q,S_h(q))\bigr)^T p_h(q)=\nabla_uJ_h(q,S_h(q)).
$$
The associated discrete-adjoint gradient vector is
$$
g_h(q):=\nabla_qJ_h(q,S_h(q))-\bigl(D_qR_h(q,S_h(q))\bigr)^T p_h(q).
$$
The next lemma proves that this vector is the gradient of $\Phi_h$; the definition itself asserts no minimizer exists and no gradient iteration converges.

An **admissibility predicate** is a specified finite-time test $\operatorname{adm}_h(q)$ that decides whether $q\in Q_h$ and checks the model's stated coefficient, boundary, mesh, and time-step hypotheses before a PDE solve. For an explicit time discretization, a Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition (CFL condition) is a method-specific bound relating the time step to the mesh and the discrete evolution operator; no universal CFL threshold is part of this definition. A true predicate result certifies that the declared model hypotheses hold for that input, not merely that a heuristic check passed.

The model must also supply an exact finite-dimensional projection routine which returns $P_{Q_h}(z)$ for a queried $z\in\Theta_h$ in finite time or reports failure only when its declared finite call budget is exhausted. The unique nearest point exists because $Q_h$ is nonempty, closed, and convex, but an operational routine for computing it is an additional part of this contract.

A solver routine with declared nonnegative state and adjoint tolerances $\tau_u,\tau_p$ and a finite solve budget must return either `failure` or approximate state and adjoint vectors $\widetilde u,\widetilde p$ together with certified finite bounds $\rho_u,\rho_p,\eta_u,\eta_p,P,L_{J,u},L_{R,u},M_q,L_{G,u}$. The residual bounds have the exact-system meaning $\|R_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{V_h}\le\rho_u$ and $\|(D_uR_h(q,u))^T\widetilde p-\nabla_uJ_h(q,u)\|_{V_h}\le\rho_p$, where $u=S_h(q)$; both must satisfy $\rho_u\le\tau_u$ and $\rho_p\le\tau_p$. In particular, an adjoint residual evaluated at $\widetilde u$ alone does not certify $\rho_p$ unless the model also bounds the resulting state and derivative-data defects. With $u=S_h(q)$ and $p=p_h(q)$, the model must certify
$$
\|u-\widetilde u\|_{V_h}\le\eta_u,\qquad \|p-\widetilde p\|_{V_h}\le\eta_p,\qquad \|p\|_{V_h}\le P,
$$
$$
\|\nabla_qJ_h(q,u)-\nabla_qJ_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{\Theta_h}\le L_{J,u}\eta_u,
$$
$$
\|(D_qR_h(q,u))^T-(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\|\le L_{R,u}\eta_u,\qquad \|(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\|\le M_q,
$$
and $\|G_h(q,u)-G_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{Y_h}\le L_{G,u}\eta_u$. It then returns
$$
\widetilde g:=\nabla_qJ_h(q,\widetilde u)-(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\widetilde p,\qquad \widetilde F:=G_h(q,\widetilde u),
$$
All constants and state/adjoint error bounds must be justified for the chosen model with every derivative-data, geometry, quadrature, and algebraic-solve defect retained. Certified residual bounds $\rho_u,\rho_p$ do not by themselves imply $\eta_u,\eta_p$; a separate model-valid stability estimate is required. The proposition below derives the resulting $\varepsilon_g$ and $\varepsilon_F$ bounds. An objective-evaluation routine must return in its finite budget either `failure` or an interval $[\ell_h(q),u_h(q)]$ containing the exact value $\Phi_h(q)$; `failure` is permitted only when a required state/adjoint solve fails its contract or the evaluation-call budget is exhausted. Exact evaluation is the degenerate-interval case. Projection and objective-evaluation calls consume the algorithm's finite evaluation budget. Each routine must return within its declared budget or report failure.

If a continuous model $F$ is also supplied, an optional mesh certificate $\varepsilon_{\rm mesh}$ must separately bound the claimed continuous-to-discrete error, such as $\|F_h(q)-F(q)\|$ or $\|\nabla\Phi_h(q)-\nabla\Phi(q)\|$. The state and adjoint algebraic residual certificates do not imply this mesh certificate.

def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot.full_current_section:
Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the counterclockwise circle $U=\{(x_1,x_2,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x_1^2+x_2^2=1\}\subset S^3=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$. Under inverse stereographic projection $x\mapsto(2x/(1+\lVert x\rVert^2),(\lVert x\rVert^2-1)/(1+\lVert x\rVert^2))$, this is the unit circle in the first coordinate two-plane of the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

Every mapped Fact uses that gluing convention, with well-definedness and reverse-mirror facts jointly supplied by separately cited items where needed.

ex-knot-kt-07-worked-cases.full_current_section:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ and $E$ be the oriented boundaries of the standard one-boundary square plumbings of two positive Hopf bands and of one positive with one negative Hopf band, respectively; these are the right-handed trefoil and the figure-eight knot. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus with unknotted core whose induced boundary components have linking number $+1$; its core, the central simple closed curve, has self-pairing $-1$. A negative Hopf band also has unknotted core and has boundary linking number $-1$ and core self-pairing $+1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the two annuli so that its edges alternate between them, then smooths the corners; use the gluing for which the resulting boundary is one component. Order the two cores $a,b$ with the positive Hopf core first, orient them so $a\cdot_F b=+1$, and use the standard plumbing side for which $a^+$ bounds a disk disjoint from $b$. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, their Seifert matrices are

$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_E=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Their determinant representatives are $\Delta_T(t)=1-t+t^2$ and $\Delta_E(t)=-1+3t-t^2$. They both evaluate to $1$ at $t=1$; at $t=-1$ the displayed representatives evaluate to $3$ and $-5$, so the unit-invariant absolute values are $3$ and $5$. These determinant classes are unchanged up to units by oriented ambient isotopy and integral basis changes. The connected sum satisfies

$$\Delta_{T\#E}(t)\doteq(1-t+t^2)(-1+3t-t^2)=-t^4+4t^3-5t^2+4t-1.$$

This displayed representative has values $1$ at $t=1$ and $-15$ at $t=-1$.
ex-knot-kt-07-worked-cases.finding: Unknotted Hopf cores are explicit; the current cited trefoil Seifert matrix is unchanged, and the current consumer Given uses exactly that positive-push matrix with full AC.

def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-hol.full_current_section:
Use the upper half-space model
$$\mathbb H^3=\{(x+iy,t):x,y\in\mathbb R,\ t>0\},\qquad ds^2=t^{-2}(dx^2+dy^2+dt^2),$$
whose ideal boundary is $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$. An oriented ideal tetrahedron in normalized position has ideal vertices $0,1,\infty,z$, where $\operatorname{Im}z>0$. Its three edge-shape parameters are
$$z,\qquad z'=\frac1{1-z},\qquad z''=\frac{z-1}{z},$$
Assign $z$ to the edges $0\infty$ and $1z$, $z'$ to $1\infty$ and $0z$, and $z''$ to $z\infty$ and $01$. The parameter at a corner of a truncated ideal vertex triangle is the parameter of the incident edge. In a triangulated oriented torus link of ideal vertices, use oriented normal paths: paths avoiding link vertices, transverse to link edges, and meeting each triangle in arcs joining distinct sides, each cutting off one corner. Represent a loop by such a path before computing its cusp multiplier. For a chosen normal path $\gamma$, its cusp multiplier $H(\gamma)$ is the product of the corner parameters it cuts off, using the parameter when the corner is on its left and its reciprocal when the corner is on its right.

The cusp proof uses these corner products; the relations consumer uses the same three parameters; the orthoscheme consumer uses only the unchanged metric and derived volume density. def-zero-surgery-on-a-knot.full_current_section: Assume countable choice as required by the chosen tubular-neighborhood and peripheral-system data. Let K be a smooth oriented knot with compact exterior E_K, positive meridian mu_K, and preferred longitude lambda_K on the boundary torus. The zero-framed surgery manifold M(K) is the closed oriented 3-manifold obtained by gluing D²×S¹ to E_K so that the meridian boundary circle of D²×{1} is identified with lambda_K and a boundary longitude {z₀}×S¹, with z₀∈∂D², is identified with mu_K. This boundary longitude is parallel inside the filling solid torus to its core {0}×S¹. The orientation extends the orientation of E_K across the filling. Thus the filling slope is the preferred zero-linking longitude; the definition asserts no 4-manifold bounded by M(K).

lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopi.full_current_section: Let $D,D'$ be nonempty finite regular oriented link diagrams related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. Let $\bar C(D)$ be the integral signed state cube before the writhe shifts, with cohomological degree $|v|$ and quantum degree $|v|+\sum\deg(a)$, and normalize it by $C(D)=\bar C(D)[n_-]\{2n_--n_+\}$ to obtain the state degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$. Before normalization, a positive type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_+)\simeq\bar C(D)\{1\}$, a negative type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_-)\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-2\}$, a type-II move gives $\bar C(D_{II})\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-1\}$, and a type-III move gives an unshifted equivalence. Consequently the normalized complexes are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. If $D,D'$ are based knot diagrams and the move disk is disjoint from the basepoint, the same chain homotopy equivalence descends to their reduced quotient complexes, equivalently to the cut-tangle complexes with interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$.

F3 is used within that Given context, so this is not an application to an empty link.

lem-odd-cube-oriented-face-parity-and-si.full_current_section: Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. If a point away from the saddle disks is marked on a component of the diagram, the vertexwise comparison commutes with its marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

ex-ip-polynomial-spectrum-risk-profile.full_current_facts_section:

[F1] Every smooth knot already contained in the standard $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$ has a regular projection under ACω. It is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and over/under data specified by strict height inequalities. [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

[F2] Under ACω, every smooth isotopy of a compact smooth manifold embedded in $S^3$ extends to an ambient isotopy. In particular, this applies to a point and to an embedded circle; each extending ambient isotopy is orientation-preserving because it starts at the identity. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

[F3] Gluing a ball-arc tangle to its reflected copy, traversed in the opposite direction, gives the oriented connected sum of the tangle's knot closure with its reverse mirror. Its oriented knot type is unchanged when either factor is replaced by an oriented ambient-isotopic representative or when the small trivial closing arc is changed. [[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]], [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

[F4] The ribbon condition requires finitely many disjoint transverse double arcs with one proper preimage arc and one interior preimage arc, and no other multiple points. [[def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot]]
lem-reverse-mirror-sum-has-a-ribbon-imme.current_claim: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere has its connected sum with its reverse mirror represented by the boundary of a smooth immersed disk in $S^3$ whose only multiple points are finitely many transverse double arcs, each having one proper preimage arc and one interior preimage arc. Consequently $K\#K^\dagger$ is ribbon in the ribbon-immersion sense.

thm-khovanov-homology-is-an-oriented-lin.full_current_facts_section:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, two finite regular diagrams of the same oriented link, and their normalized cochain complexes.

[F1] AC$_\omega$ is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under AC$_\omega$, diagrams of the same oriented link are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] Every planar isotopy and oriented Reidemeister I, II or III move induces a bigraded chain homotopy equivalence of the normalized complexes ([[lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopies]]).

[F4] A bounded cochain complex has defined cohomology in each bidegree, and chain homotopy equivalent complexes induce isomorphic cohomology ([[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]], [[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]]).
thm-khovanov-homology-is-an-oriented-lin.current_claim: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $L$, the bigraded integral groups $Kh^{i,j}(L):=H^i(C^{*,j}(D))$, where $D$ is any finite regular oriented diagram of $L$ and $C(D)$ is the normalized Khovanov cochain complex, are independent of the choice of $D$ up to bigraded isomorphism.

lem-odd-marked-reidemeister-i-ii-contrac.current_claim: For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

**Given:** An RIII disk, the exterior resolution cubes, and a mark outside the disk.

[F2] Full face prescriptions exist, compare by vertex signs, and include the oriented-intersection prescription on zero-composite faces ([[lem-odd-cube-oriented-face-parity-and-sign-existence]]).

lem-odd-marked-reidemeister-iii-common-c.current_claim: For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

lem-based-odd-barnatan-movie-maps-and-lo.full_current_facts_section:

[F1] The odd and Bar–Natan algebras, maps, state gradings and mod-two identification are those in [[def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple]]. The Bar–Natan Frobenius identities and square-zero equation are proved there.

lem-based-odd-barnatan-movie-maps-and-lo.current_claim: Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-pr.full_current_facts_section:
**Given:** Countable choice, the knots and their chosen oriented Seifert surfaces, and the fixed oriented connected-sum convention.

[F2] [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]] fixes the oriented connected-sum convention, and [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]] identifies the resulting knot type independently of the local gluing choices.

The hypotheses apply to knots in $S^3$. The theorem is stated over $\mathbb Z$; tensoring its chain maps, inverse maps, and homotopies with $\mathbb F_2$ preserves their identities. Its tensor filtration on homogeneous generators gives the convolution filtration displayed in the Statement. I read the theorem and its proof sketch; the proof constructs the standard triangle map and refers to Ozsváth–Szabó, *Holomorphic disks and three-manifold invariants: properties and applications*, §6, for the ordinary connected-sum map. I read that section through Theorem 6.2, but do not claim to reconstruct the knot-filtration adaptation stated in Theorem 7.1.

Hom's threshold definition in §3.1 is the same least filtered level as [F1]; its target is $\widehat{HF}(S^3)\cong\mathbb F_2$, so “nonzero image” and “surjective” agree. The survey states on printed p. 2 that it works throughout with $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients. I read the definition and theorem statement; I do not claim to reconstruct the theorem's cited proof.
lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-pr.current_claim:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces $F_K$ and $F_J$. Use the boundary-connected-sum surface $F_K\natural F_J$ to normalize the connected-sum model. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$
